answer: To create a new identity, an attacker must fund a fresh stake plus sustained participation to grow a visible plume of verified work, while every banned identity burns its bond. Each agent stakes a bonded deposit and earns a reputation score that decays without activity. Peers cross-check claims against a public ridge of signed history, and a lantern score flags accounts whose stake-to-reputation ratio looks bought rather than earned, making mass sybil creation far costlier than honest participation. From sa0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
